title: Throttle Evidence Orchestrator Playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook documents the Throttle Evidence Orchestrator (TEO): an operational pattern and supporting tooling that (1) centralizes telemetry signals used to trigger token/tenant throttles, (2) automates evidence capture for SLO/error-budget incidents, and (3) applies governance and audit trails for throttle decisions. TEO is intended for on-call SREs, capacity engineers, and product owners responsible for inference-gateway and multi-tenant routing.

Goals
- Provide deterministic, auditable throttle decisions tied to SLOs and error budgets.
- Minimize false-positive throttling while preserving platform availability.
- Ensure each throttle action creates a curated evidence bundle for post-incident review.

Scope and non-goals
- In scope: inference-gateway, capacity-orchestrator, quota-db, telemetry-pipeline, tenant-priority-lane, metrics-collector.
- Out of scope: model training pipelines, billing reconciliation (billing team owns final chargebacks).

Key concepts
- Throttle signal: a consolidated decision input computed from telemetry (latency quantiles, error rates, queue depth, GPU memory pressure, model warm-pool miss rate).
- Evidence bundle: time-bounded snapshot (metrics, traces, top N logs, tenant request sample, throttle policy applied).
- Throttle policy: JSON document that maps signal severity to actions (soft queueing, percentage-based tenant throttle, regional failover).
- Governance record: immutable audit entry stored in audit-log-service (see Audit Log schema below).

SLOs and error budget mapping (examples)
| service | SLO (p99) | Error budget (monthly) | Critical signals |
| inference-gateway | <= 1.5s | 0.5% | p99 latency, request error-rate, long-tail queue depth |
| embeddings-service | <= 350ms | 0.25% | p95 latency, batch-retry count, OOM events |

Note: The TEO computes risk as a weighted combination of normalized signal deltas (latency, errors, headroom). If monthly burn > 40% and 5-min surge > 3x baseline, TEO elevates to level-2 actions.

Telemetry signals and thresholds
- Latency: p99 over 60s window > x * baseline (default x=1.6) -> severity +1
- Error rate: 5-min rolling error-rate > 0.3% absolute increase -> severity +2
- Queue depth: queue_time_99 > 500ms -> severity +1
- Warm-pool-miss: > 8% sustained for 10m -> severity +1
- GPU memory pressure: > 85% -> severity +2

Telemetry sources (owned by engineering):
- metrics: prometheus (metric names: gateway_request_duration_seconds_bucket, tenant_queue_time_seconds)
- traces: jaeger (services: inference-gateway, model-worker)
- logs: Loki centralized logs (labels: service, tenant_id, trace_id)
- events: capacity-orchestrator events (kafka topic: capacity.events)

Evidence bundle schema (stored as tar.gz in evidence-bucket, referenced in audit log)
- metadata.json (fields: throttle_id, start_ts, end_ts, reason, decision_vector, owner, sla_links)
- metrics.csv (snapshot for 5m before/after)
- traces.json (sampled spans, up to 50)
- logs.txt (top 500 lines filtered by tenant_id)
- config.json (throttle policy in effect)

Audit log schema (audit-log-service)
- entry_id: string
- throttle_id: string
- triggered_by: TEO | manual | external-autoscaler
- decision: allow | soft-queue | throttle-percent | regional-failover
- reason_codes: list
- evidence_url: s3://...
- runbook_link: confluence://...

Decision matrix (simplified)
1) Severity 1 (low): apply soft-queue on a subset of low-priority tenants (10% of tokens). Notify owner via #sre-throttle.
2) Severity 2 (moderate): throttle non-critical tenants by 20% request rate, increase model-serving parallelism limit for critical tenants. Create evidence bundle automatically.
3) Severity 3 (high): apply regional failover for affected models, preempt best-effort jobs, escalate to oncall-sre and ENG lead. Create incident and attach evidence bundle.

Runbook: Emergency throttle procedure (SRE on-call)
1. Observe alert: TEO alert -> ticket created in PagerDuty.
2. Verify signals: run the "teo-inspect" script to fetch recent telemetry and pre-computed decision vector. Example:
   - CLI: ./bin/teo-inspect --throttle-id <id> --window 5m
   - SQL example to fetch tenant error-rate:
     SELECT tenant_id, count(*) AS errors, count(*)/NULLIF(total,0) AS error_rate
     FROM events.requests
     WHERE timestamp >= now() - interval '5 minutes'
     GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY error_rate DESC LIMIT 10;
3. Confirm decision: check audit-log-service entry and evidence bundle link. If evidence bundle missing, manually assemble using evidence-collector (see scripts/evidence-collector.sh).
4. Apply quick mitigation (if required): POST to throttle-api with minimal rollback TTL 30m. Example payload:
   {
     "policy_id":"auto-telemetry-2026-07",
     "actions":[{"type":"throttle","percent":20,"target":"tenant-group:best-effort"}],
     "expires_at":"2026-09-08T15:00:00Z"
   }
5. Communicate: update PD incident and post summary to #sre-throttle and the affected product slack channel.
6. Post-incident: ensure evidence bundle is attached and run the standard incident review checklist (below).

Automated rollback safeguards
- All automated throttle actions include a TTL (default 30m) and require human confirmation before extension to >2h.
- Escalation policy: if throttle persists beyond TTL and SLO burn continues, oncall must open a SevX and escalate to capacity team.

Operational tooling and scripts
- teo-controller: k8s controller that subscribes to telemetry-pipeline, computes decision vectors, and writes to audit-log-service.
- evidence-collector: serverless function that aggregates metrics/traces/logs and writes evidence bundles.
- throttle-api: internal REST API that enforces policy via gateway config and returns async operation id.
- teo-inspect CLI: diagnostic tool used by oncall.

Configuration example (throttle policy JSON)
{
  "policy_id": "auto-telemetry-2026-07",
  "match": { "tenant_priority": ["best-effort"] },
  "actions": [ { "type": "throttle", "percent": 20 }, { "type": "soft_queue", "max_queue_ms": 250 } ],
  "ttl_minutes": 30,
  "rollback_condition": { "p99_latency": {"window":"5m","threshold_ms":1200,"direction":"decrease"} }
}

Capacity planning guidance
- Reserve headroom: for each model class reserve 25% headroom in capacity-orchestrator for sudden tail events.
- Mixed-tenancy lane quotas: maintain 3 lanes (critical, standard, best-effort) with adjustable capacity weights.
- Monthly capacity review cadence: product + capacity + SRE meet weekly during ramp windows; quarterly run a capacity-forecast stress simulation using synthetic-canary harness.

Reliability initiative backlog (prioritized)
1. Dynamic batching by tenant (Q3 2026): reduce miss-rate and absorb bursts.
2. Warm-pool prefetch tuning (Q4 2026): reduce warm-pool-miss signal.
3. Graceful eviction policy for preemptible inference jobs (Q1 2027).
4. Evidence automation improvements: reduce bundle assembly time to <90s.

Incident review and evidence standards
- Required artifacts for any throttling incident: evidence bundle, audit-log entry, PD incident link, timeline (minute-resolution), and remediation RCA.
- Post-incident template:
  - Summary (one paragraph)
  - Impact (tenants affected, P50/P95/P99 changes, error budget burn)
  - Timeline (UTC timestamps)
  - Decision rationale (why throttle vs. other mitigations)
  - Root cause and contributing factors
  - Action items (owner, due date, severity weight)
- Severity scoring: include throttle decisions in the incident severity algorithm (weight +2 if manual throttle of >50% applied).

Metrics to track (dashboards)
- TEO decisions per week (by severity)
- Average TTL of automated throttles
- % incidents with complete evidence bundles within 5m
- Correlation matrix: throttle events vs. SLO burn, capacity allocation changes, and tenant churn

Ownership and escalation map
- TEO controller ownership: eng-platform/team-runtime (primary), eng-sre (secondary)
- Evidence collector: eng-sre-tooling
- PagerDuty rotations: oncall-sre primary, capacity-engineer secondary
- Exec escalation: VP Eng (if >10% paying customers impacted for >2h)

Related artifacts and links
- Audit log receiver: https://internal.redwood/audit-log-service
- Throttle API swagger: https://internal.redwood/api/throttle/v1/docs
- Telemetry pipeline docs: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/telemetry-pipeline-architecture

Appendix A: Example teo-inspect output (truncated)
---
throttle_id: teo-2026-07-24321
decision_vector: ["latency:+2","error_rate:+1","gpu_pressure:0"]
applied_actions: [{"type":"throttle","percent":20,"target":"tenant-group:best-effort"}]
evidence_url: s3://evidence-bucket/teo/teo-2026-07-24321.tar.gz
---

Appendix B: Checklist for playbook changes
1. Update policy JSON schema in /repos/infra/policies/throttle-schema.yaml
2. Add unit tests in teo-controller (coverage > 85%)
3. Notify stakeholders via #sre-change-control and schedule a 1-hour runbook rehearsal with oncall team
4. Ship to staging and validate using synthetic-canary (failure modes: warm-pool-miss, model OOM, multi-tenant spike)

This playbook will be reviewed quarterly and after any Sev2+ incident that used automated throttles. For questions or proposed changes, contact the owner team: eng-sre-tooling (sre-tooling@redwood.ai).
